runs.text: Cimpress's leverage rose in the latest quarter and is not yet pro forma for its acquisition. Total debt principal was USD 1,667.6 million at September 30, 2026, equal to 3.71x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 449.6 million, against 3.57x at FY2026, and net debt to EBITDA rose to 3.44x from 3.03x as cash fell from USD 248.9 million to USD 120.1 million. The July 2026 Saxoprint acquisition cost USD 131.6 million net of cash acquired and was funded from cash and a USD 35.0 million revolver drawing; trailing EBITDA holds only the post-closing contribution, which the filing calls not material, and acquired pre-closing EBITDA is not supplied [CP-1; CP-1A transaction summary]. This is documentary fact.

The earnings trend is the central weakness. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 89.8 million in Q1 FY2027 against USD 98.7 million a year earlier, with revenue up 8% to USD 934.1 million but only 2% on an organic constant-currency basis. Cost of revenue rose to 56.3% of revenue from 53.3% on start-up costs for the North American network, depreciation, tariffs and energy, partly offset by a USD 7.5 million tariff refund [CP-1A operating model]. Adjusted EBITDA also adds back USD 61.4 million of share-based compensation in FY2026; if that add-back is treated as a cost, total leverage at FY2026 is 4.12x rather than 3.57x [CP-1 calculations]. This is Analyst Interpretation built on documentary figures.

Earnings are concentrated. VistaPrint produced USD 392.6 million of USD 642.1 million segment EBITDA in FY2026, or 61.1%, with gross margin of about 55% (management's approximate figure) and low working capital because customers pay before production [CP-1A operating model]. The Upload and Print segments, at about 32% gross margin, drive growth and acquisitions but contribute less profit per revenue dollar. A fall in VistaPrint advertising efficiency or tariff costs would therefore move group EBITDA more than any other single factor.

Cash generation has weakened but still covers interest. Adjusted free cash flow, which is after cash interest, was USD 122.4 million in FY2026 against USD 148.0 million in FY2025 and USD 261.1 million in FY2024, and USD 130.9 million on the trailing twelve months. EBITDA covered cash interest 4.11x on the trailing twelve months and 4.18x in FY2026 [CP-1 interest cover and metrics tables]. The interest burden is partly floating: USD 1,129.5 million of variable-rate debt means a 100 basis point rise would add USD 7.4 million to annual interest expense, with swaps on a USD 350.0 million notional already accruing [CP-1 facility terms].

Liquidity is adequate but seasonal. Cash plus undrawn revolver was USD 317.8 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 120.1 million cash and USD 197.7 million of revolver availability), down USD 163.7 million from USD 481.6 million at June 30, 2026 [CP-1 liquidity table]. The first quarter builds inventory and receivables ahead of the December peak, and the December quarter carries most annual profit [CP-1A operating model]. Obligations due within one year, including interest, leases and purchase commitments, were USD 278.9 million.

Refinancing risk is distant but has a trigger. Scheduled amortisation is USD 11.5 million to USD 18.5 million a year and USD 1,570.6 million falls due after FY2031, mostly the USD 525.0 million 7.375% senior notes due September 15, 2032 and the term loan due June 4, 2033. The 10-Q adds that the term loan matures earlier, on June 16, 2032, if the notes have not been repaid, refinanced or extended, which the 10-K does not state; the credit agreement is not supplied to settle this [CP-1A conflicts log]. The practical maturity wall is therefore mid-2032.

Covenant protection is limited. The only maintenance covenant is a Consolidated Leverage Ratio not above 4.50x, tested only when revolving usage exceeds 20% of commitments at a quarter end; usage was 14.0% at September 30, 2026, so the test did not apply and management states compliance with all covenants. The reported covenant ratio and its EBITDA definition are not printed, so headroom cannot be calculated [CP-1]. Protection therefore rests on collateral for the secured facility and on incurrence and restricted-payment limits that are not visible in the supplied sources.

Capital allocation is equity-oriented. Management states its uppermost objective is intrinsic value per share, repurchased USD 284.8 million of shares over FY2024 to FY2026 and authorised a further USD 200 million in March 2026, with none used in Q1 FY2027 [CP-1A governance table]. No dividend, priming, uptiering or debt-funded distribution is documented, so the behaviour category is Neutral or Mixed rather than Extraction-Oriented or Creditor-Adverse, but legal capacity cannot be tested without the documents.

Claims outside the reported debt figure add to effective leverage. Finance leases of USD 56.0 million, supply chain finance of USD 58.8 million within payables, unrecorded purchase commitments of USD 310.3 million, redeemable noncontrolling interests of USD 78.4 million and a USD 9.6 million put due in Q2 FY2027 sit outside the USD 1,667.6 million. Including finance leases, total leverage on the trailing twelve months is 3.83x [CP-1].

runs.text: Strengths. Cimpress has a profitable, cash-collected flagship in VistaPrint, which serves about 11 million small businesses a year with an average order value of about USD 100 and produced 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA, so revenue visibility rests on a very large number of small orders rather than a few customers [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact, with the order-value figures as Management Language]. It has maintained cash interest cover of 4.11x and positive adjusted free cash flow of USD 130.9 million over the trailing twelve months despite lower margins [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. It refinanced the 2026 notes with 2032 notes in FY2025 and extended the secured facility to 2033 and 2031 in June 2026, which leaves no sizeable scheduled maturity for several years [CP-1A transaction summary; Documentary Fact]. Liquidity of USD 317.8 million and a revolver only 14.0% drawn leave room under the springing covenant [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Disclosure is transparent, with reconciliations of adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow [CP-1A; Documentary Fact].

Weaknesses. Leverage of 3.71x total and 3.44x net on issuer-defined EBITDA is rising, and 4.12x if share-based compensation is treated as a cost [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Margins are under pressure from tariffs, energy, depreciation and plant start-up, and Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA is lower than a year ago despite an acquisition [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. Earnings are concentrated in one brand and one quarter [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Capital allocation prioritises repurchases, with an unused USD 200 million authorisation, while restricted-payment baskets are unknown [CP-1A governance table; Documentary Fact for the history, Insufficient Information for the covenant capacity]. The structure has a springing term loan maturity in 2032 tied to the notes, an unresolved acquisition price and sale-leaseback status, and significant debt-like claims outside reported debt [CP-1A conflicts log; Documentary Fact]. Ownership percentages and control rights are not disclosed beyond a statement that the top 10 holders own about 70% [CP-1A company profile; Insufficient Information].

runs.text: Saxoprint and viaprinto. On July 2, 2026 Cimpress acquired the Saxoprint and viaprinto businesses of CEWE Stiftung & Co. KGaA, a subsequent event to the FY2026 10-K period and part of Q1 FY2027. The September 2026 10-Q states total purchase consideration of $141,081 (US$141.1m; €123,996), funded in cash from the available cash balance and the senior secured revolving credit facility (10-Q Sep 2026 page:18). Business acquisitions net of cash acquired were 131,557 (10-Q Sep 2026 page:4) and revolver borrowings were 35,000 (page:21). The preliminary allocation records goodwill of 36,480, intangible assets of 22,471 in total, and assets held for sale of 46,449 (page:19); final values are expected in the second quarter of FY2027. The business is managed within PrintBrothers, and its revenue and earnings in the quarter are described as not material. The 10-K, written after closing, stated the price as €120,000 subject to a post-closing adjustment and said no definitive sale-leaseback agreement had been executed (10-K pages:70, 142); the 10-Q says a plan to market and execute a sale-leaseback of the manufacturing facility was approved in Q1 FY2027 and the asset is held for sale (10-Q Sep 2026 page:19). Status: closed; sale-leaseback planned, not evidenced as signed. Liquidity effect: cash fell from 248,851 to 120,127 over the quarter (CP-1).

Credit agreement amendment and restatement, June 4, 2026. The Restated Credit Agreement increased the Term Loan B by 35,289 to cover fees and increase liquidity, issued at 99.75% of par, extended the term loan to June 2033 and the revolver to June 2031, with no other material changes (10-K page:118). Costs: debt issuance costs of 7,789 and a discount of 2,750 capitalised, and a loss on early extinguishment of 3,722 for FY2026 (10-K page:119). Status: executed and effective. The agreement itself is not supplied. At September 30, 2026 the Term Loan B was 1,094,500 and the revolver commitment 250,000 with 35,000 drawn (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21).

7.375% Senior Notes due 2032. Issued under an indenture dated September 26, 2024 with certain subsidiaries as guarantors (10-K page:147); FY2025 proceeds of 525,000 and payments for early redemption or purchase of 7.0% Senior Notes due 2026 of 522,135 (10-K page:89; FY2025 column). Debt issuance costs of 11,658 were capitalised in FY2025 (10-K page:119). The notes are unsecured, pay semi-annual coupons on March 15 and September 15, and are redeemable at the indenture's prices (10-Q Sep 2026 pages:22, 47). Use of proceeds: refinancing of the 2026 notes, per the cash flow lines; the offering document is not supplied.

PrintBrothers minority sale, FY2026. A minority 8.75% interest in each PrintBrothers business was sold to members of management for cash of 24,814 (€21,000), with a 10-year lock-up and a put right from 2036; the redeemable interest was recorded at fair value 61,498 (€53,000), with a share-based compensation asset of 36,684 (10-K page:131). This adds a long-dated equity-like claim that can become a cash call from 2036; it also shows funding of the business from management, not from lenders.

Subsequent put exercise. Minority holders of one smaller business exercised a put; the purchase of their shares will cost 9,602 in Q2 FY2027 (10-Q Sep 2026 page:24). Status: committed, not yet paid at September 30, 2026.

Prior debt in the period: Q1 FY2027 borrowings of 100,848 and repayments of 69,529 (10-Q Sep 2026 page:5), consistent with the revolver draw and term loan amortisation. No new bond issue, rating action, or exchange offer is reported after June 30, 2026 within the supplied filings; the earnings releases that might describe later events are unreadable. Nothing after 2026-11-05 is used.

Perimeter: the consolidated group of Cimpress plc as printed in the 10-K and 10-Qs. Cimpress plc is the single registrant and issuer of the 7.375% Senior Notes due 2032; the senior secured facility has several borrowers (see 10-K page:150), and no separate borrower-level statements are supplied, so every metric below is group-level. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial base is adequate for downstream credit work, with stated limits. Reported statements for FY2024, FY2025, FY2026, Q1 FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 are complete and their expense blocks reconcile to operating income. On the issuer's own adjusted EBITDA, total debt to EBITDA was 3.70x at FY2025, 3.57x at FY2026 and 3.71x on the trailing twelve months to September 30, 2026; net debt to EBITDA was 3.16x, 3.03x and 3.44x. EBITDA to cash interest was 3.93x, 4.18x and 4.11x. The movement in the latest period is explained by the July 2026 Saxoprint acquisition, which was funded from cash and revolver borrowings, while trailing EBITDA contains only the post-acquisition months and Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA fell year on year. In US$m: total debt principal 1,667.6, cash 120.1, liquidity 317.8 (June 30, 2026: 481.6), share-based compensation added back in FY2026 61.4, and adjusted free cash flow 122.4 in FY2026 (FY2025: 148.0). Three limits bind every metric: adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's measure and adds back share-based compensation, the covenant definition and reported ratio are not supplied, and debt excludes finance leases, supply chain finance and purchase commitments, which are shown separately.

fields.value: - Leverage and acquisition effect. Between June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026 debt principal rose by 31,227 thousand while cash fell by 128,724 thousand, because Saxoprint cost 131,557 thousand net of cash acquired and was funded from cash and 35,000 thousand of revolver borrowings (10-Q Sep 2026 pages:4, 21). Net leverage therefore rose to 3.44x from 3.03x, while LTM EBITDA holds only the post-acquisition part of the new business and its pre-acquisition EBITDA is not supplied. The first-quarter adjusted EBITDA decline (89,820 against 98,715) came mainly from higher start-up costs for the North American network, tariff costs and depreciation, partly offset by a 7.5 million tariff refund benefit (10-Q Sep 2026 page:33). Run-rate leverage after acquired EBITDA and any sale-leaseback proceeds cannot be derived from the sources.

fields.value: - Quality of EBITDA. Issuer adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based compensation (61,379 in FY2026, 13.4% of FY2026 adjusted EBITDA) and deducts realised losses on currency hedges (14,169). Treating share-based compensation as a cost gives FY2026 EBITDA of 397,119 and total leverage of 4.12x; on LTM figures 387,106 and 4.31x. The hedge programme targets adjusted EBITDA to maintain stability on debt covenants (10-Q Sep 2026 page:50), so adjusted EBITDA is plausibly close to the covenant definition, but that cannot be confirmed without the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash generation. Operating cash flow fell from 350,722 (FY2024) to 283,706 (FY2026) while capital spending, including capitalised software, rose to 167,290 in FY2026. Issuer adjusted free cash flow, which is after cash interest because operating cash flow includes interest paid (10-Q Sep 2026 page:34), fell from 261,053 to 122,432. In FY2026 cash was also used for acquisitions of 32,390, share repurchases of 50,077, withholding taxes on equity awards of 19,313 and finance lease payments of 11,740 (10-K pages:89-90). A buyback authorisation of 200 million remains (10-Q Sep 2026 page:52); none was used in Q1 FY2027, and share repurchases are restricted payments under the secured facility (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was 317.8 million against 481.6 million at June 30, 2026. Contractual obligations falling due within one year total 278,887 thousand including interest, leases and purchase commitments (10-Q Sep 2026 page:45). The second fiscal quarter is the peak season; the first-quarter working capital outflow was 23.7 million (10-Q Sep 2026 page:44).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Maturities and refinancing. Scheduled amortisation is small (11.5 to 18.5 million a year), with 1,570.6 million due after FY2031. The Term Loan B springs to June 16, 2032 unless the 2032 Notes are repaid, refinanced or extended, so the practical wall is the 525.0 million note refinancing in 2032.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt-like claims outside the debt figure. Finance leases of 56,003, operating lease payments of 157,858 (undiscounted fixed), supply chain finance of 58,781 inside accounts payable, purchase commitments of 310,257 (cloud services 192,636), redeemable noncontrolling interests of 78,361 (a put exercised by minority holders of one small business will require 9,602 in the second quarter of FY2027), and pension liabilities of 9,060. Including finance leases, total leverage is 3.83x on LTM figures. Book equity is a deficit of 479,409 after cumulative share repurchases (treasury shares at cost 1,363,550).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant. A maintenance test of Consolidated Leverage Ratio not above 4.50x applies only if revolving loans, swingline loans and unreimbursed letter of credit disbursements exceed 20% of commitments at a fiscal quarter end (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21). On the printed 35,000 of loans against 250,000 of commitments, usage was 14.0%, so the test was not triggered at September 30, 2026; 15,000 of further drawings would reach the 20% threshold. Management states compliance with all covenants (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21). The covenant ratio itself is not printed.

Operating income reconciles to gross profit less the expense block of technology, marketing, general and administrative, intangible amortisation and restructuring for all five periods. The adjusted EBITDA bridges recompute to the printed figures. Debt principal by instrument sums to the printed total at each date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cimpress is a decentralised group of web-to-print and promotional-product businesses run by a small central team, financed with a covenant-light structure of a secured term loan and revolver plus unsecured notes. The creditor-relevant business facts are that one brand, VistaPrint, supplies most segment EBITDA with high gross margin and low working capital; that the Upload and Print segments earn lower margins but are growing faster and are the acquisition platform; that profits are concentrated in the December quarter; and that U.S. tariffs, energy and North American capacity start-up costs are compressing margin. The transaction facts are a June 2026 amendment that extended maturities, and a July 2026 acquisition of Saxoprint and viaprinto that was funded from cash and the revolver and moved leverage higher. Governance is equity-oriented rather than sponsor-driven: management states that maximising intrinsic value per share is its uppermost objective and has repurchased shares every year in the periods supplied, but the filings document no priming, uptiering, dividend or debt-funded distribution. On the evidence in the pack the behaviour category is Neutral or Mixed: transparent reporting and an extension of maturities beside steady repurchases and an unresolved acquisition funding plan. Ownership percentages, control rights and sponsor history are not supplied; the filing says about 70% of shares are held by the top 10 shareholders without naming them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Saxoprint and viaprinto. On July 2, 2026 Cimpress acquired the Saxoprint and viaprinto businesses of CEWE Stiftung & Co. KGaA, a subsequent event to the FY2026 10-K period and part of Q1 FY2027. The September 2026 10-Q states total purchase consideration of $141,081 (US$141.1m; €123,996), funded in cash from the available cash balance and the senior secured revolving credit facility (10-Q Sep 2026 page:18). Business acquisitions net of cash acquired were 131,557 (10-Q Sep 2026 page:4) and revolver borrowings were 35,000 (page:21). The preliminary allocation records goodwill of 36,480, intangible assets of 22,471 in total, and assets held for sale of 46,449 (page:19); final values are expected in the second quarter of FY2027. The business is managed within PrintBrothers, and its revenue and earnings in the quarter are described as not material. The 10-K, written after closing, stated the price as €120,000 subject to a post-closing adjustment and said no definitive sale-leaseback agreement had been executed (10-K pages:70, 142); the 10-Q says a plan to market and execute a sale-leaseback of the manufacturing facility was approved in Q1 FY2027 and the asset is held for sale (10-Q Sep 2026 page:19). Status: closed; sale-leaseback planned, not evidenced as signed. Liquidity effect: cash fell from 248,851 to 120,127 over the quarter (CP-1).

fields.value: CIMPRESS plc, as of 2026-11-05, credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the fundamental credit view, built from the financial base and the business and transaction context of the pinned filings (10-K for FY2026 and three 10-Qs, latest for Q1 FY2027). Peer ranking, instrument recommendation and recovery conclusions are out of scope.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cimpress is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative high yield credit whose financial risk rose in the latest quarter because a debt-funded acquisition coincided with margin pressure. Its strongest support is the VistaPrint brand, which earned 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA, together with USD 317.8 million of liquidity and small scheduled maturities until the notes and term loan fall due in 2032 and 2033. The weakest point is margin: adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 89.8 million in Q1 FY2027 from USD 98.7 million while total debt reached USD 1,667.6 million, or 3.71x trailing EBITDA. What decides the outcome is whether margins recover through the December peak season and whether cost actions and any sale-leaseback proceeds reduce net debt before the 2032 refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cimpress's leverage rose in the latest quarter and is not yet pro forma for its acquisition. Total debt principal was USD 1,667.6 million at September 30, 2026, equal to 3.71x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 449.6 million, against 3.57x at FY2026, and net debt to EBITDA rose to 3.44x from 3.03x as cash fell from USD 248.9 million to USD 120.1 million. The July 2026 Saxoprint acquisition cost USD 131.6 million net of cash acquired and was funded from cash and a USD 35.0 million revolver drawing; trailing EBITDA holds only the post-closing contribution, which the filing calls not material, and acquired pre-closing EBITDA is not supplied [CP-1; CP-1A transaction summary]. This is documentary fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The earnings trend is the central weakness. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 89.8 million in Q1 FY2027 against USD 98.7 million a year earlier, with revenue up 8% to USD 934.1 million but only 2% on an organic constant-currency basis. Cost of revenue rose to 56.3% of revenue from 53.3% on start-up costs for the North American network, depreciation, tariffs and energy, partly offset by a USD 7.5 million tariff refund [CP-1A operating model]. Adjusted EBITDA also adds back USD 61.4 million of share-based compensation in FY2026; if that add-back is treated as a cost, total leverage at FY2026 is 4.12x rather than 3.57x [CP-1 calculations]. This is Analyst Interpretation built on documentary figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are concentrated. VistaPrint produced USD 392.6 million of USD 642.1 million segment EBITDA in FY2026, or 61.1%, with gross margin of about 55% (management's approximate figure) and low working capital because customers pay before production [CP-1A operating model]. The Upload and Print segments, at about 32% gross margin, drive growth and acquisitions but contribute less profit per revenue dollar. A fall in VistaPrint advertising efficiency or tariff costs would therefore move group EBITDA more than any other single factor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation has weakened but still covers interest. Adjusted free cash flow, which is after cash interest, was USD 122.4 million in FY2026 against USD 148.0 million in FY2025 and USD 261.1 million in FY2024, and USD 130.9 million on the trailing twelve months. EBITDA covered cash interest 4.11x on the trailing twelve months and 4.18x in FY2026 [CP-1 interest cover and metrics tables]. The interest burden is partly floating: USD 1,129.5 million of variable-rate debt means a 100 basis point rise would add USD 7.4 million to annual interest expense, with swaps on a USD 350.0 million notional already accruing [CP-1 facility terms].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate but seasonal. Cash plus undrawn revolver was USD 317.8 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 120.1 million cash and USD 197.7 million of revolver availability), down USD 163.7 million from USD 481.6 million at June 30, 2026 [CP-1 liquidity table]. The first quarter builds inventory and receivables ahead of the December peak, and the December quarter carries most annual profit [CP-1A operating model]. Obligations due within one year, including interest, leases and purchase commitments, were USD 278.9 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is distant but has a trigger. Scheduled amortisation is USD 11.5 million to USD 18.5 million a year and USD 1,570.6 million falls due after FY2031, mostly the USD 525.0 million 7.375% senior notes due September 15, 2032 and the term loan due June 4, 2033. The 10-Q adds that the term loan matures earlier, on June 16, 2032, if the notes have not been repaid, refinanced or extended, which the 10-K does not state; the credit agreement is not supplied to settle this [CP-1A conflicts log]. The practical maturity wall is therefore mid-2032.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant protection is limited. The only maintenance covenant is a Consolidated Leverage Ratio not above 4.50x, tested only when revolving usage exceeds 20% of commitments at a quarter end; usage was 14.0% at September 30, 2026, so the test did not apply and management states compliance with all covenants. The reported covenant ratio and its EBITDA definition are not printed, so headroom cannot be calculated [CP-1]. Protection therefore rests on collateral for the secured facility and on incurrence and restricted-payment limits that are not visible in the supplied sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation is equity-oriented. Management states its uppermost objective is intrinsic value per share, repurchased USD 284.8 million of shares over FY2024 to FY2026 and authorised a further USD 200 million in March 2026, with none used in Q1 FY2027 [CP-1A governance table]. No dividend, priming, uptiering or debt-funded distribution is documented, so the behaviour category is Neutral or Mixed rather than Extraction-Oriented or Creditor-Adverse, but legal capacity cannot be tested without the documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the reported debt figure add to effective leverage. Finance leases of USD 56.0 million, supply chain finance of USD 58.8 million within payables, unrecorded purchase commitments of USD 310.3 million, redeemable noncontrolling interests of USD 78.4 million and a USD 9.6 million put due in Q2 FY2027 sit outside the USD 1,667.6 million. Including finance leases, total leverage on the trailing twelve months is 3.83x [CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Cimpress has a profitable, cash-collected flagship in VistaPrint, which serves about 11 million small businesses a year with an average order value of about USD 100 and produced 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA, so revenue visibility rests on a very large number of small orders rather than a few customers [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact, with the order-value figures as Management Language]. It has maintained cash interest cover of 4.11x and positive adjusted free cash flow of USD 130.9 million over the trailing twelve months despite lower margins [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. It refinanced the 2026 notes with 2032 notes in FY2025 and extended the secured facility to 2033 and 2031 in June 2026, which leaves no sizeable scheduled maturity for several years [CP-1A transaction summary; Documentary Fact]. Liquidity of USD 317.8 million and a revolver only 14.0% drawn leave room under the springing covenant [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Disclosure is transparent, with reconciliations of adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow [CP-1A; Documentary Fact].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage of 3.71x total and 3.44x net on issuer-defined EBITDA is rising, and 4.12x if share-based compensation is treated as a cost [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Margins are under pressure from tariffs, energy, depreciation and plant start-up, and Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA is lower than a year ago despite an acquisition [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. Earnings are concentrated in one brand and one quarter [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Capital allocation prioritises repurchases, with an unused USD 200 million authorisation, while restricted-payment baskets are unknown [CP-1A governance table; Documentary Fact for the history, Insufficient Information for the covenant capacity]. The structure has a springing term loan maturity in 2032 tied to the notes, an unresolved acquisition price and sale-leaseback status, and significant debt-like claims outside reported debt [CP-1A conflicts log; Documentary Fact]. Ownership percentages and control rights are not disclosed beyond a statement that the top 10 holders own about 70% [CP-1A company profile; Insufficient Information].
